Subject: Three things your trails need from you this autumn
CTA: Find a trail stewardship event near you -> https://www.northbaysupply.com/trail-stewardship
Body: Hey,

Autumn is the stretch where a lot of trail damage quietly sets itself up for spring. The ground is still workable now. A few hours outside with the right intentions goes a long way.

Three things worth doing before the ground freezes:

**1. Clear the drainage before the leaves do it for you.**
Water moving off the tread is everything. Walk your local trail after a rain and look for spots where runoff is cutting across instead of away. Clear debris from waterbars and check that dips in the tread are actually lower than the edges. A plugged waterbar doesn't announce itself until you're looking at an eroded channel in May.

**2. Don't shortcut the shortcuts.**
Fall foot traffic tends to widen social trails — people stepping around mud, around roots, around each other. If you see a shortcut forming at a switchback corner, block the entry with a few natural rocks or downed wood. It doesn't have to be tidy. It just has to redirect the first few steps.

**3. Flag, don't fix, what's beyond a day's work.**
If you find a section that needs a crew — a failing turnpike, a major blowdown across the tread, a crumbling retaining structure — photograph it, note the GPS coordinates, and report it to your local trail association or land manager. Fixing it incorrectly can compound the problem. Reporting it accurately means the people with the right tools and authority can plan a proper work day before conditions close the window.

Trails that go into winter in decent shape come out of it in decent shape. That's the whole logic here.

See you out there.
